# Freelance Tax Notes

Personal reminders for filing taxes as a freelance designer.

## Quarterly estimated payments

Estimated tax payments are due on April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15. Set aside about thirty percent of every client invoice in a separate savings account. Pay online through the government payment portal and keep the confirmation number for each payment.

## Deductible expenses

Home office costs are deductible when the space is used only for work. Track the square footage of the office as a share of the apartment. Software subscriptions, a new monitor, and professional training courses are deductible. Client dinners are only fifty percent deductible, so keep receipts with the name of the client written on them.

## Mileage log

Record the date, destination, purpose, and kilometers for every business trip. The standard mileage rate for this year is 0.67 per kilometer. A spreadsheet synced to the cloud is enough, as long as entries are made at the time of the trip.

## Invoicing

Send invoices with net-30 payment terms and add a two percent late fee after forty-five days. Number invoices sequentially, for example 2026-014, and always include the client tax identification number.

## Accountant meeting

Meet the accountant, Mr. Okafor, in early February with the profit and loss summary, the mileage log, and all receipts sorted by month. Ask him about the retirement contribution limit and whether a home office depreciation schedule is worth setting up.
